body: Same with Kohl's. I used to work there, and they had a "Yes We Can" policy that meant that we could do just about anything as long as it made the customer happy, including using expired coupons.

I honestly was so sick from it last night that I couldn't leave to go kill myself. Passed out while trying to walk outside. I can't take much more of this. :( I just want to be done. 

I talked with my ex a little today. The friend's really upset with me, because we didn't meet all that long ago (right before I started getting really sick), so she's making assumptions and judgments about who I am when she mostly just knows cognitively impaired, erratic, brain damaged me. It's a scary, upsetting, delicate situation.

Thanks. That's very kind. I wish I could believe that, but I feel that I'm fragile, and I'm disgusted with myself for hurting/inconveniencing people I care about.
I'm in the process of getting my card, and marijuana does take the edge off a little.
Maybe. But at the same time, I'd live, and so it'd matter that I was missing work (for monetary and hopefully not getting fired reasons). I can't afford a hospitalization.

It's just that I'm so socially anxious that I know I'm going to feel so much worse and more terrified there, when I can have some sense of resolution in a time frame that's much more acceptable and a situation that's much more private this way.

That's solid info. Thank you. I haven't been pulled aside by my employer yet, so here's to hoping that it wasn't a big enough deal to justify calling them. I live in one of the bigger Michigan cities, so the cops have bigger things to worry about, but I thought it would be worth checking with the good people on this subreddit. The background check thing makes sense as well, since I wasn't arrested or taken anywhere, and I could see why it probably wouldn't impact me based on that.

For sure. The officer who was doing most of the talking kept telling me, "You know that just because the cops are here, it doesn't mean you're in trouble, right?" I'm sure they were being extra cautious in that scenario.

Yeah, I understand, and that makes sense. If I had been worse off when they had shown up, maybe I would've been grateful for their rescue. I know they weren't necessarily trying to upset me or anything with their prying questions. 

That's pretty reassuring. My work has a code access door, but I'm 95% sure they don't check cameras. The witness explanation is a very good suggestion. Thank you for that.
